value.body: A physical education teacher runs PE classes, games periods and fitness activities in a school, and trains school teams for competitions. Employers are government and private schools, and residential and sports schools. A day mixes outdoor classes, team practice, event organising and some record keeping.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.P.Ed (often after a B.P.E.S. or other degree)

items.label: Government posts
items.value: PET / PGT Physical Education through state and central teacher recruitment

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Private schools hire directly, usually asking for a B.P.Ed. Government school posts are filled through state teacher-recruitment exams or boards, which set their own qualification rules; some also need a teacher eligibility test.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Teaching games and fitness to groups

value.title: At a glance
items: Most schools have only one or two PE posts.
Recruitment rules for government posts differ by state.
Next roles: senior PE teacher, sports coordinator, or college teaching after an M.P.Ed.
